overall_summary: The channel's top-performing content leverages extreme cosmic anomalies and paradoxical science facts (e.g., burning ice, space smells, ancient sharks) to trigger high curiosity. Conversely, abstract psychology and generic brain facts struggle to gain traction. Maintaining a consistent 16-second duration with highly sensory, counter-intuitive hooks is currently the most reliable path to maximizing views.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet of Burning Ice Will Break Your Brain!' (1,053 views), 'The Largest Ocean in Space Will Mind-Blow You!' (460 views), and 'What Does Outer Space Actually Smell Like?' (368 views) are the channel's top performers.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on space facts that feature extreme physical contrasts, unusual sensory details (smells, tastes), or seemingly impossible physics.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'Sharks Are Older Than Trees?' (302 views) and 'This Animal Literally Dies Every Winter!' (179 views) outperform standard animal trivia.
winning_patterns.action: Frame biological facts around shocking timeline comparisons or extreme survival mechanisms that challenge common assumptions.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' (38 views) and 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (54 views) consistently underperform.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid generic 'your brain' hooks. If presenting psychology, anchor the hook in a highly specific, relatable behavior rather than abstract neuroscience.

next_video.concept: The exoplanet where it literally rains liquid iron at night.
next_video.opening_direction: Start with: 'There is a giant planet in space where it literally rains molten iron from the sky...'
next_video.twist_direction: Explain that on WASP-76b, daytime temperatures are so extreme they vaporize metal, which then condenses and falls as iron rain on the cooler night side.
next_video.reason: This concept perfectly mirrors the 'extreme cosmic paradox' formula of the channel's top-performing video ('The Planet of Burning Ice') by using strong sensory imagery (iron rain) to drive immediate retention.

experiment: Test a 15-second historical timeline paradox video (e.g., comparing the construction of the Pyramids to the existence of Woolly Mammoths) to see if history-based timeline anomalies can replicate the high engagement of cosmic anomaly videos.
